residue.text: Replay the finite schedules independently; compare registrations, distinct recognitions, actions, queue identities, duplicates, delivery times and dashboard boundaries. Missing registration, recognition below eight, a seventh action, or an interruption duplicate defeats operational success. This can separate present exposure and deadline performance; it cannot distinguish later-demand causation, which is excluded from this window.

Both proposed schedules spend six validation ticks and six dispatcher actions; readable ledgers add no clerk labor. Interruption predicts seven processed entries. The audited sham generates nine entries and processes eight within the window. Extra actions, servers, channels, repair and configuration are unavailable. Neither schedule has an observed successful execution.

Delay origin, sender adaptation and global schedule optimality remain unknown. A hypothetical later comparison requires attributable new status-query notices and comparable sender conditions. A later difference would still need exclusion of exogenous differences.

summary.text: Hold eight initial notices fixed. Six registrations and seven distinct recognitions remain; registration and recognition are separate outputs. Requests at tick 8 cannot count. No new demand arrives during this window.

Proposed interruption suppresses receipts for already recognized identities. Validate N3,N4,N5,N6,N7,N8 at ticks 0,1,2,3,4,5. Individually request N2,N3,N4,N5,N6 at ticks 0,1,2,3,4; bulk at 6 requests N7,N8. Predicted deliveries are N2 through N6 at 1 through 5, N7 at 7 and N8 at 8: eight registrations, eight recognitions, six actions.

Stage1 sham proposes the same validations, bulk at 0, individuals N3,N4,N5,N6 at 2,3,4,5, then bulk at 6. Its forecast of eight recognitions overlooks N6 still pending at boundary 6 before its tick-6 delivery. Bulk therefore also enqueues N6. Model audit predicts duplicate N1 at 1, N2 at 2, N3 through N6 at 3 through 6, duplicate N6 at 7, N7 at 8; N8 misses the deadline. This sham fails the fixed outcome and is not a matched successful control.

Retain both hypotheses without selecting: exogenous later demand predicts similar added status-query demand despite reduced repeated-receipt exposure; tool-induced later demand predicts less added demand after interruption than sham under comparable later conditions. Both predict zero added demand here. Equal later demand after verified exposure reduction would oppose the induced account. No later observations establish either account; present duplicate harm does not prove later adaptation.
